To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the form factors of nucleon transfer in inelastic collisions can be calculated by a microscopic model, and that these form factors are similar to those of inelastic scattering.

(1) The correlation lengths for nucleon transfer are systematically larger than those for inelastic scattering, and increase with distance from the nucleus; (2) The form factors are sensitive to the angular momentum transfer, which can be as large as 8h units; (3) The form factors for nucleonic transfer are similar to those for inelastic nucleon scattering.
The nucleon transfer process in deeply inelastic scattering can be described in terms of a microscopic calculation based on the shell model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a microscopic calculation of the form factor in the nucleon transfer process.
a microscopic description of nuclear processes at the level of the nucleon-nucleon interaction.
the study of the nucleon transfer mechanism in the deep inelastic collisions of heavy ions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present calculations are in good agreement with experimental data, although there are still many details that require further study.
in the present model the transfer of angular momentum is not a dominant feature in the process of nucleon transfer.
the form factors for the transfer of nucleons are in good agreement with the predictions of the microscopic model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nucleon transfer process is dominated by a large number of nucleons in the overlap region, which are strongly correlated in their relative motions.
inelastic nucleon-transfer is a process of the type in which the nucleus is broken up into its constituents, the nucleons, and the nucleons are scattered inelastically from each other.
a microscopic theory can describe the form factors for deeply inelastic collisions as well as for inelastic scattering.
